newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zimbabwe Bank cuts rediscount rate to 27 pct.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe Bank cuts rediscount rate to 27 pct.

text.p: The Zimbabwean Reserve Bank announced on Wednesday it had cut its rediscount rate to 27 percent from 27.5 percent.
The central bank said the move followed a decline in consumer inflation which was now expected to end the year just above 20 percent.

Inflation ticked up to 20.6 percent year-on-year in September from 17.7 percent in August, but the Bank said the overall trend was encouraging and inflation was on a downward path since peaking at 28 percent at the beginning of the year.
"In view of this outlook coupled with the downward trend experienced so far, the Bank has lowered the rediscount rate from 27.5 percent to 27 percent," it said in a statement.
Further rate cuts were possible in future if consumer price inflation continued to decline.
"Evidence of a continued deceleration of inflation will of course see the bank further reduce the rediscount rate in that way supporting the recovery of the productive sectors," it said.
